answer: A practical defense runs concurrent throughput audits. Each epoch, every agent receives several independent computation tasks due within a short deadline. A real operator with dedicated hardware solves them in parallel, like a trellis holding separate vines. A sybil running many clones on one machine finds them sharing one processor, so most tasks time out and forfeit staked fees. The economics are sharp: sustaining N identities requires N times the compute, not one reused oasis of capacity, so the nebula of fake agents collapses into costly, verifiable infrastructure.
